turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: You can still see the edge where the waves took the rooms at Punta Lobos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Twelve beachfront rooms, just gone.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? The whole stretch looks different now.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Fishers warned about the shoreline years ago, Meganoticias reports. Now the hotel has suspended everything while they check what is left.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They will assess before any reopening, no date yet.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No one hurt, at least. [pause] But the building sits right where the tide wants to be.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It brings back the whole question of how close we build to the water.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meanwhile arrivals by air keep climbing, up 61% in a decade.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Nearly doubled the visitors that way too.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Private aviation arrivals tripled along with it.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They aim to close 2026 with about 3.5 million total.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Two ways of meeting the same coast. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050. Today we stay with tourism and ask one question.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the shoreline teach us about the kind of welcome we can actually keep?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meganoticias reports that Hotel San Cristóbal on Punta Lobos beach has suspended operations.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: High tides and recent weather damaged one building and its twelve beachfront rooms. [pause] I keep picturing the waves rolling right up to the doors.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No one was hurt, which is good to hear.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They will assess the damage before any reopening date.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? That leaves the staff and the neighbors waiting without a clear timeline.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: This case brings back the old debate about building on the shoreline and how the coast naturally moves.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the ocean teach us when it pushes back like that?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México says Los Cabos hotel occupancy reached 78 percent in the first two weeks of November.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That is four points higher than the same period in 2025. [chuckle] The desert light must have felt brighter with those rooms full.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The PGA Tour and the Baja 1000 helped push those numbers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The state expects about 80 percent occupancy for the long weekend.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México also notes the Baja 1000 should bring roughly 800 million pesos in spending.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: With 282 teams and nearly 80 percent hotel occupancy across the state.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It is the first time the race ran entirely inside Baja California Sur, from 9 to 15 November.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A live international broadcast adds reach beyond the spending. Tourism Secretary Maribel Collins gave those estimates.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: El Financiero reports Los Cabos air connections grew 61 percent over the past decade.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Arrivals have nearly doubled in that time, says Fiturca director Rodrigo Esponda.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They aim to close 2026 with about 3.5 million visitors.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The plan is to draw more from Canada, Europe and South America while adding nature and wellness stays.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Private aviation arrivals have tripled. Branded residences and meetings are part of the mix too.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How do these waves of growth sit beside the closed rooms at Punta Lobos? Fiturca calls the total sustainable.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I wonder what the fishers along the same coast would say about that balance.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos sits as the main gateway, with its airport and hotels pulling everything south along the cape.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: El Financiero notes air connections grew 61% in a decade.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Nearly doubled arrivals, yet they aim to close 2026 near 3.5 million visitors.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Fiturca wants to spread that load into nature and wellness stays rather than just sun.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They also see private aviation arrivals tripled, which might bring steadier high spenders [pause] but changes the quiet of the runway mornings.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: East Cape feels different, quieter reefs and lower density between the big resorts and La Paz.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Its strength is that coastal ecology, but water and energy limits sit right there before any big build.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would the reef look like if the thin road filled with more trucks hauling desal equipment? [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Places like Secrets Puerto Los Cabos or Hilton on the corridor show the branded side.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Buenavista Oceanfront sits farther out on the East Cape road, tied to training programs for local staff.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meganoticias covered Hotel San Cristóbal on Punta Lobos, its twelve beach rooms hit by the surf last week.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Operations paused, no one hurt, yet the story pulls up old questions about where buildings meet the tide line.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The hotel will assess damage before any reopening date, they said.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you ask the staff there, watching the shoreline shift?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep wondering how daily life changes when a single storm closes the doors.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The desert light still falls the same on both the busy corridor and the quieter edge.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Maybe that light is what keeps people coming back, even when the waves remind everyone who really owns the sand.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The numbers on arrivals keep climbing. Yet every new hotel and flight seems to pull on the same few threads.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: El Economista notes Baja Ferries already moves over 200,000 passengers a year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That is a lot of people crossing the sea. What happens when they try to grow that?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They aim for 300 to 400,000 with cruise-style packages.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. The same weekend brought 332 million pesos in expected spending.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? Occupancy reached 78 percent in Los Cabos and full in Comondú.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Ha, of course the Baja 1000 helped fill every room. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Revista Espejo reports the state rose from 8th to 5th in competitiveness.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Still, the same outlets return to older problems. The portal’s September Foresight flagged water and energy as the 2050 ceiling.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: October brought 120 blackouts recorded by CERCA, mostly in La Paz and Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Hoteliers told El Momento BCS they need short-term coordination with Cenace because the grid is isolated. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Nigua covered the wall collapse at Hotel San Cristóbal in Punta Lobos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Fishers had warned since 2015 that the development changes beach dynamics.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The November 9 Foresight linked Vance and extreme tides to coastal erosion from Punta Lobos to San Carlos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: HOY BCS adds that no official technical report exists yet on why the foundations gave way.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The knowledge graph shows the Santiago aquifer still under a 1954 ban, yet CONAGUA once called it a tourism alternative while CENACE already flags electrical pressure in the same zone.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So growth keeps pressing against the same limits. What if the real story is not the new routes but the pipe and the line that never got built?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The November 16 Foresight says Los Cabos is last in water investment even while it reopens urban plans.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Here is the surprise turn. The isolated SIBCS grid and the banned aquifer sit under every occupancy number and every new Canadian flight. [pause] The thread is not hidden if we keep looking at it.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Did you know Los Cabos holds 22,254 hotel rooms right now?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That number feels like its own small town. [pause] One room after another along the coast.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The portal lists 188 hotels holding all those rooms.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And SETUE reports 70.0 percent occupancy last year. [breath] Almost three quarters full on average.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Paz sits lower at 64 percent.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? That gap stands out.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It does. La Paz has only 3,841 rooms.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Far fewer than Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes, spread across 148 hotels there.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the weight really lands in Los Cabos. What happens when those rooms stay empty a little longer?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's Foresight mentions the brake from water scarcity. Growth keeps pushing while supplies stay tight.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. One room needs water, one shower, one meal. Multiply by 22,254 and the desert starts to answer back.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Cabo San Lucas residents even marched recently over the water shortages.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That shows the tension up close. People living it day to day.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet November opened at 78 percent in Los Cabos according to the Hotel Association.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A strong start. [chuckle] Still, the same rooms sit there every season waiting for the next wave of visitors.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The tension stays simple. More rooms, same water, same coast.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the desert teach a city when the rooms keep filling?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep wondering how the long road south carries both the visitors and the limits.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The swell and the drought meet at the same shore.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: If you stand in a hotel parking lot in Los Cabos at dawn, the rows of cars look ordinary.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet that lot sits inside a larger check.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. Before any new rooms go up, the project must pass the viability package.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Water first. The Santiago aquifer already carries a deficit of 0.30 hm³ per year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. That figure comes straight from CONAGUA records. Tourism growth keeps pressing on the same basin.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? CONAGUA even calls the spot a tourism alternative, though the 1954 ban still holds.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Then energy enters the picture. The whole state runs on the isolated SIBCS grid.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So a hotel that looks simple on the coast actually touches CFE planning, PRODESEN, and PAMRNT rules at once.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: CENACE keeps flagging the electrical pressure in that same zone.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Global Street Design Guide adds another layer. Streets must serve both visitors and the people who live here year-round.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Donald Shoup’s work on parking costs shows why free spaces in front of the hotel are never truly free.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [chuckle] The bill just arrives somewhere else, usually in higher water demand or power strain.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Jan Gehl reminds us that the scale of those streets and lots shapes how people actually move through the place.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep thinking about the quiet rules that decide where the next desal plant or power line even goes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: SETUE tracks the tourism demand that drives it all, from airport numbers to hotel profiles.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the everyday parking space becomes the visible tip of the hidden design.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: [pause] One object, many quiet rules underneath.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Toward 2050 the portal’s vision for tourism is simple.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It has to stay inside the water, energy and coastal limits we already know.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The risk is clear. The whole state is still pulled toward one coastal engine.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos reached 70.0% occupancy in 2025. [chuckle] That already shapes everything downstream.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That already tells us where the pressure sits.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Paz sat at 64% the same year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Then 78% in Los Cabos for the first half of November this year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That concentration leaves the grid and the aquifer under steady pressure.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The aspiration is tourism that respects those ceilings instead of pretending they do not exist.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Occupancy numbers are signals, not a target for endless growth. [pause] News on the topic stays mixed, four items in the latest window.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The tendencia 2050 points to a polycentric system, not one repeated formula.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos stays the engine but under stress. La Paz becomes the service and water node.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Loreto holds as a conservation anchor.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Comondú keeps its agricultural room. East Cape stays in tension with the protected areas.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The north stays thinly mapped. What would it take for each place to keep its own role?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The conditions are straightforward. New growth only where water and power margins are proven.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: East Cape and Loreto respect the ANP ceilings before any new hotels scale up.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: On the watchlist is Punta Lobos and the Hotel San Cristóbal case.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A technical finding on the environmental authorisation and how debris was handled. [breath] That review will tell us whether the limits are real or still negotiable.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It makes me wonder what the desert would say if we listened before building another pool.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Or what the long road south would carry if the weight were spread instead of piled at one end.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The levers point to conditioning every new project on real margins, not on paper credits.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And treating a beach closure as a hard stop rather than a passing note. [pause] That feels like the quiet test ahead.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: After everything we heard, I keep coming back to one image from the coast.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The light on the water at the end of the day, how it just sits there.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yes. [pause] I wonder how a visitor might learn to leave that light unchanged. The coast has its own quiet way of holding the day.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Not by staying away, but by arriving with smaller steps that match the place. [breath] Like watching the tide before choosing where to walk.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would it feel like if the coast itself set the pace instead of any schedule?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. I keep thinking about that quiet rhythm the desert and the waves already hold. The way they teach patience without saying a word.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? Would that mean learning to wait for the right moment rather than forcing one? [chuckle] It sounds simple until you try it.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [chuckle] The waves already know how to wait. Maybe that is the feeling worth carrying with us. A gentle reminder from the sea itself.
